title: Gowers half product
statement: Let $F$ be a real-valued family on pairs consisting of a binary vector of length $k+1$ and a point of the $n$-dimensional binary cube. Choose a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,k\}$, a bit $b\in\mathbb{F}_2$, a point $x$ of the $n$-dimensional binary cube, and a $k$-tuple $y$ of such points. The Gowers half product is the product, over all binary vectors $s$ of length $k$, of $F$ evaluated at the vector obtained by inserting $b$ into $s$ at coordinate $i$ and at the Gowers cube point associated to $x,y,s$.
caveat: The definition of the Gowers cube point is not included in the supplied payload, so its construction cannot be stated more explicitly.
